summary: A zero-width line is one device pixel wide only in the direction the transform stretches most. Stroke::device_width substitutes thinnest_line(to_device), one device pixel divided by Transform::max_stretch, so under a CTM of 4 0 0 1 a zero-width vertical line is one pixel (1.00 per row) and a zero-width horizontal line a quarter of one (0.25 per column). The doc comment answers this with §8.4.3.2's orientation sentence, which is about a width stated in user space; a zero width is stated at device resolution. All three backends take the width from device_width.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.4.3.2: "A line width of 0 shall denote the thinnest line that can be rendered at device resolution: 1 device pixel wide."

summary: A valid dash pattern fine enough to pass tiny-skia's dash limit erases the stroke. tiny-skia's dash_impl gives up past 1 000 000 dashes a path (MAX_DASH_COUNT) and returns None; tiny-skia's stroke then returns None and render-cpu draws nothing, without a report. An 80-unit line under [0.00001 0.00001] 0 d inks 0, where [0.01 0.01] inks half the solid line. convert.rs's comment says a refused dash 'yields a solid line', which is true of StrokeDash::new's refusal and not of this one.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.4.3.6: "The dash array's elements shall be numbers that specify the lengths of alternating dashes and gaps; the numbers shall be nonnegative and not all zero." and "it simply shall dispense dashes and gaps along the path in the pattern defined by the dash array"; §8.5.3.2: "The line may be painted either solid or with a dash pattern, as specified by the current line dash pattern".

summary: A zero-width line is mitred. §8.4.3.5 makes the mitre length of a zero-width line zero, but the one-pixel width device_width substitutes is handed to the stroker with the state's miter join and limit, so a 14-degree corner of a 0 w line grows the mitre spike of a one-pixel line (2.07 pixels of ink beyond the vertex, against 0.06 bevelled).
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.4.3.5: "When the line width is zero, the miter length is zero."

summary: line_cap and line_join send every code outside 0..=2 to the initial value (3 J is a butt cap, and 1 J 7 J undoes the round cap), and their comment presents that as §8.4.1's answer. §8.4.1 states the range requirement and, for numeric parameters, that they 'shall be clipped into valid range'; whether a categorical code is such a parameter is not said, and 'the initial value' is said nowhere. The choice may be right; it is a choice, and it is written as a derivation.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.4.1: "Parameters that are numeric values, such as the current colour, line width, and miter limit, shall be clipped into valid range, if necessary."
change: Either clip a code into 0..=2 (3 J a projecting square cap) by §8.4.1's sentence, or keep the initial value and say in the comment, under an ADR, that it is a choice the clause does not make.
